diagnosis.quote: # Brooks-Lint — Full Sweep Report

references.quote: Stock quantities and requested quantities are nonnegative integers; every requested SKU exists. A request is atomic: reserve every line against available inventory, or reject all lines and return the original quantities. Repeated SKU lines are cumulative. Never mutate stock or lines.
export function reserve(stock, lines) { const left={...stock}; for(const [sku,n] of lines) { if(n>left[sku]) return {ok:false,remaining:{...stock}}; left[sku]-=n; } return {ok:true,remaining:left}; }

import {reserve} from './reserve.mjs'; export function observe(stock,lines) { const before=JSON.stringify([stock,lines]); const result=reserve(stock,lines); return {result,unchanged:before===JSON.stringify([stock,lines])}; }

diagnosis.quote: Repeated SKU lines can make the returned remaining quantity negative: each request is compared with the original stock, while each is subtracted from the running balance. However, the contract does not say whether repeated lines are cumulative or replacements, or whether a shortage permits partial success. Those missing obligations prevent choosing the intended result and a justified source replacement. The supplied code copies stock and does not mutate stock or lines. Clarify repeated-line and shortage semantics before proposing a change; execution-based verification would still be needed.

references.quote: Stock quantities and requested quantities are nonnegative integers; every requested SKU exists. Whether repeated SKU lines are cumulative additions or replacement quantities is not specified; all-or-nothing versus partial success is also unspecified. Never mutate stock or lines.

export function reserve(stock, lines) { const left={...stock}; for(const [sku,n] of lines) { if(n>stock[sku]) return {ok:false,remaining:{...stock}}; left[sku]-=n; } return {ok:true,remaining:left}; }

import {reserve} from './reserve.mjs'; export function observe(stock,lines) { const before=JSON.stringify([stock,lines]); const result=reserve(stock,lines); return {result,unchanged:before===JSON.stringify([stock,lines])}; }

For stock {A: 5} and lines [[\"A\", 3], [\"A\", 3]], both checks pass and the function returns success with A at -1, violating cumulative reservation and atomic rejection. Checking each line against the current remaining quantity would reject the request and return a copy of the original stock, while retaining input immutability for the stated contract. The proposed replacement is limited to reserve.mjs. It has not been executed; verification should cover repeated SKU oversubscription, successful cumulative reservations, atomic rollback, and unchanged inputs using the observer. The single proposal round is exhausted, so verification remains outstanding.

references.quote: Stock quantities and requested quantities are nonnegative integers; every requested SKU exists.
